title: Why Planes Get a Bath Before Winter Flights
sources: FAA AC 120-60 'Ground Deicing and Anti-icing Program' / FAA AC 20-117 'Hazards Following Ground Deicing and Ground Operations in Conditions Conducive to Aircraft Icing' / NASA Glenn 'A Pilot's Guide to Ground Icing' / AOPA 'Icing' safety spotlight: frost, ice or snow with the thickness and roughness of medium or coarse sandpaper on a wing's leading edge and upper surface can reduce lift by as much as 30 percent and increase drag by about 40 percent
14 CFR 121.629 (eCFR) / 14 CFR 135.227 / FAA AC 120-60 'clean aircraft concept': no person may take off when frost, ice or snow is adhering to the wings, control surfaces or propellers

FAA 'Holdover Time Guidelines' (2025-26 / 2026-27 tables, General Information) / Wikipedia 'Aircraft deicing fluid' / Transport Canada TP 10643 'Deicing/Anti-icing Fluids': Type I fluid is a glycol-and-water mix, low-viscosity, usually dyed orange and applied heated to remove frost, ice and snow; it gives only short protection (minutes) in falling snow

FAA Holdover Time Guidelines / NASA Glenn 'A Pilot's Guide to Ground Icing' / Wikipedia 'Aircraft deicing fluid': Type IV anti-icing fluid is thickened (gel-like), dyed green, applied cold after deicing, keeps new snow and ice from sticking for a holdover time (the estimated time the protection lasts), and is designed to shear off the wing during the takeoff roll

Aviation Pros 'Deicing and Anti-Icing Equipment' / Des Moines Register 'Behind the scenes of de-icing planes at the Des Moines International Airport': de-icing trucks with a boom and an operator's bucket spray the aircraft, often on a dedicated de-icing pad
NASA Glenn 'A Pilot's Guide to Ground Icing': surface roughness disturbs the smooth airflow over the wing's upper surface, lowering lift and the stall angle

lines.text: If you leave a jet out on a cold night, its wings can forget how to fly.
lines.caps: If you leave a jet out | on a cold night, | its wings can forget | how to fly.

lines.text: By morning, a thin coat of frost covers them, as rough as sandpaper.
lines.caps: By morning, a thin coat | of frost covers them, | as rough as sandpaper.

lines.text: But that roughness can steal up to thirty percent of the lift.
lines.caps: But that roughness | can steal up to 30% | of the lift.

lines.text: So, the rule is simple: no takeoff with frost, ice, or snow stuck to the wings.
lines.caps: So, the rule is simple: | no takeoff with frost, | ice, or snow | stuck to the wings.

lines.text: Before departure, the jet rolls onto a de-icing pad.
lines.caps: Before departure, | the jet rolls | onto a de-icing pad.

lines.text: A worker in a bucket on a truck's boom sprays it with hot, orange fluid.
lines.caps: A worker in a bucket | on a truck's boom | sprays it with | hot, orange fluid.

lines.text: It's mostly glycol and water, and it melts the frost right off.
lines.caps: It's mostly glycol and water, | and it melts the frost | right off.

lines.text: But if snow keeps falling, the wing can ice up again within minutes.
lines.caps: But if snow keeps falling, | the wing can ice up again | within minutes.

lines.text: So, a second coat goes on: a thick, green gel that keeps new snow from sticking.
lines.caps: So, a second coat goes on: | a thick, green gel | that keeps new snow | from sticking.

lines.text: Pilots get a time limit, called holdover time, to take off.
lines.caps: Pilots get a time limit, | called holdover time, | to take off.

lines.text: But wouldn't goo on the wing ruin the flight, too?
lines.caps: But wouldn't goo | on the wing | ruin the flight, too?

lines.text: No. As the jet races down the runway, the wind shears the gel right off.
lines.caps: No. As the jet races | down the runway, | the wind shears | the gel right off.

lines.text: You see, a wing only lifts when air flows smoothly over its curved top.
lines.caps: You see, a wing only lifts | when air flows smoothly | over its curved top.

lines.text: That's why, on a winter morning, your plane gets a bath before it flies.
lines.caps: That's why, on a winter morning, | your plane gets a bath | before it flies.
